title: 🟡 P2 — `compact --before` under-deletes expired traces when the writer's UTC offset differs from the host's: traces are compared as RFC3339 STRINGS against a locally-offset cutoff while flows are compared by absolute time, so 5h of expired traces survive (measured: 144,004 traces kept vs 98,410 flows kept = 1.463x; traces floor 07:42:24Z, flows floor 12:42:23Z — same instant, one cut)

The two floors are the same moment in time; the trace floor is exactly 5h too early = the host's UTC offset. 45,594 expired traces survive a compaction that deleted their parent flows, so they are unreachable from any flow view but still counted by trace-level aggregates. /api/v1/stats then reports a permanently skewed total_traces/total_flows ratio (1.463x here) and the DB never reaches the size the user asked for.

FIX: compare absolute time on both tables (unixepoch()/julianday() or compare against a UTC cutoff string with a uniform offset) and make flow/trace deletion use the same predicate; add a test with writer-offset != host-offset.
